# Replication


## Stata

- Downloaded code and data from dropbox.
- unzipped all the necessary datafiles. 
- Ran the master do-file as per README, in Stata. Master do-file did not run smoothly in one go, I had to make some minor changes:


### p04_Sample_Creation.do

- The authors said they found the issue in the block between lines 584 and 632 and solved it. However, I am now expierincing a new error `__000001 not found`. For some years, no survival rate data exists in the OECD dataset. When the code filtered for a specific year using `keep if TIME == ${year}`, this resulted in a dataset with 0 observations. This caused Stata to crash with the error `__000001 not found`, because `egen mean()` can't run on an empty dataset. Additionally, `saveold` saved an empty file, which then caused the merge in `stack_data` to fail.

To fix this, I added a `count` check after the merges. If the dataset is empty, I create a placeholder dataset with the correct variable structure but 0 observations. If data exists, the `egen` averages are computed as normal. This solved the issue, the code ran fine afterwards. 

```stata
count
if r(N) == 0 {
    clear
    set obs 1
    gen iso3_o = ""
    gen SurvivalRate1 = .
    gen SurvivalRate2 = .
    gen SurvivalRate3 = .
    gen SurvivalRate1_average = .
    gen SurvivalRate2_average = .
    gen SurvivalRate3_average = .
    drop in 1
}
else {
    egen SurvivalRate1_average = mean(SurvivalRate1)
    label var SurvivalRate1_average "Average OECD 1-year survival rate"
    egen SurvivalRate2_average = mean(SurvivalRate2)
    label var SurvivalRate2_average "Average OECD 2-year survival rate"
    egen SurvivalRate3_average = mean(SurvivalRate3)
    label var SurvivalRate3_average "Average OECD 5-year survival rate"
}
```
- Furthermore, the README states that all TRAIN zip files must be manually unzipped before starting the replication. However, the code apparently already performs the unzipping, so this instruction can either be removed or adjusted accordingly?

```stata
unzipfile "TRAINS`year'.zip", replace
local files : dir "`c(pwd)'" files "*TRAINS`year'*.dta"

```

## Matlab

- Downloaded code and data from dropbox.
- unzipped all the necessary datafiles. 
- Ran the scripts per README. Most of the scripts ran fine and without any error. 

`Master_script_gravity_v3.m`: Code seem to run fine and was able to generate some output but crashed at some point. I tried to run in multiple times but Matlab constantly shuts down at some point. I ran this part with 16CPUs and 64GB memory. As a result, I can't located figures OA.13,14,15 & 16 in my output. 

`LinearCF_wrapper_v3.m`: Code seems to run fine, however looking at the output it seems to generate only a few files. Figure 6, Table 1, and Figures OA.29–OA.31 and Table OA.6 could not be located.

`run_mc_master.m` ran with 16 CPUs and 64GB of memory but Matlab constantly breaks down at the run_gmm step due to insufficient memory. Therefore, I was not able to replicate this part of the replication.

## Other Issues

The authors have significantly improved the README. As noted in the report, I encountered difficulties when running several of the Matlab scripts. This might partly be due to the limited computational capacity of the Nuvolos applications (at least for the Monte Carlo script), it would be helpful if the authors could verify the other two scripts, as they were able to generate some output but crashed afterwards. 



# Classification

As stated earlier in the report I was not able to complete the necessary scripts for the data preparation and was therefore not able to produce any output. 

- [ ] full reproduction
- [ ] full reproduction with minor issues
- [x] partial reproduction (see above)
- [ ] not able to reproduce most or all of the results (reasons see above)

## Reason for incomplete reproducibility

- [ ] None.
- [x] `Discrepancy in output` (either figures or numbers in tables or text differ)
- [x] `Bugs in code` that were fixable by the replicator (but should be fixed in the final deposit)
- [ ] `Code missing`, in particular if it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
  - [ ] `Data preparation code missing` should be checked if the code missing seems to be data preparation code
- [ ] `Code not functional` is more severe than a simple bug: it prevented the replicator from completing the reproducibility check
- [ ] `Software not available to replicator` may happen for a variety of reasons, but in particular (a) when the software is commercial, and the replicator does not have access to a licensed copy, or (b) the software is open-source, but a specific version required to conduct the reproducibility check is not available.
- [ ] `Insufficient time available to replicator` is applicable when (a) running the code would take weeks or more (b) running the code might take less time if sufficient compute resources were to be brought to bear, but no such resources can be accessed in a timely fashion (c) the replication package is very complex, and following all (manual and scripted) steps would take too long.
- [ ] `Data missing` is marked when data *should* be available, but was erroneously not provided, or is not accessible via the procedures described in the replication package
- [ ] `Data not available` is marked when data requires additional access steps, for instance purchase or application procedure. 
- [ ] `Missing README` is marked if there is no README to guide the replicator, or the README is not in compliance with JPE requirements
